audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar Miriam, Aaron, Moses, and Cushite-wife narrative tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Cushite-wife criticism, prophetic authority, Moses' humility, Divine speech, Miriam's skin affliction, Aaron's confession, Moses' healing prayer, seven-day exclusion, and communal waiting. Strong anti-racism, anti-misogyny, anti-authoritarian, and anti-stigma safeguards required.

verses.restored: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses concerning the Cushite woman whom he had taken, for a Cushite woman he had taken.

familiar.text: And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.

verses.restored: They said, Has YHWH indeed spoken only through Moses? Has he not also spoken through us? And YHWH heard.

familiar.text: And they said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

verses.restored: Now the man Moses was very humble/meek, more than every human upon face of ground.

familiar.text: (Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)

verses.restored: Suddenly YHWH said to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam, You three go out to tent of meeting. And the three went out.

familiar.text: And the LORD spake suddenly unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, Come out ye three unto the tabernacle of the congregation. And they three came out.

verses.restored: YHWH came down in pillar of cloud and stood at entrance of tent, and called Aaron and Miriam; the two went forward.

familiar.text: And the LORD came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam: and they both came forth.

verses.restored: He said, Hear, please, my words: If there is a prophet among you, I YHWH make myself known to him in vision; in dream I speak with him.

familiar.text: And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the LORD will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.

verses.restored: Not so my servant Moses; in all my house he is faithful.

familiar.text: My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.

verses.restored: Mouth to mouth I speak with him, plainly and not in riddles, and form of YHWH he beholds. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?

familiar.text: With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

verses.restored: Anger of YHWH burned against them, and he departed.

familiar.text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against them; and he departed.

verses.restored: Cloud turned away from over tent, and look, Miriam was afflicted with scale-disease, white as snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam, and look, she was afflicted.

familiar.text: And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.

verses.restored: Aaron said to Moses, Please, my lord, do not place upon us sin/misalignment in which we acted foolishly and in which we sinned.

familiar.text: And Aaron said unto Moses, Alas, my lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sin upon us, wherein we have done foolishly, and wherein we have sinned.

verses.restored: Please do not let her be like one dead, whose flesh is half consumed when coming out from mother's womb.

familiar.text: Let her not be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he cometh out of his mother’s womb.

verses.restored: Moses cried to YHWH, saying, El, please heal her, please.

familiar.text: And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, If her father had spit in her face, would she not bear shame seven days? Let her be shut outside camp seven days, and afterward she shall be gathered in.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again.

verses.restored: Miriam was shut outside camp seven days, and people did not set out until Miriam was gathered in.

familiar.text: And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.

verses.restored: Afterward people set out from Hazeroth and camped in wilderness of Paran.

familiar.text: And afterward the people removed from Hazeroth, and pitched in the wilderness of Paran.

translation_notes: The Cushite woman must not be demeaned or treated as the cause of impurity. The text gives no license for racism, anti-Blackness, xenophobia, or condemnation of interracial marriage.
Miriam and Aaron both speak, but only Miriam receives the visible affliction. This gender asymmetry must remain under ethical and reception-history critique.
Moses' unique prophetic role in this narrative does not create blanket immunity from accountability; Torah elsewhere records challenges, failures, and correction of leaders.
The affliction is rendered scale-disease/skin affliction rather than modern Hansen's disease.
Moses' brief prayer, El na refa na lah, centers healing rather than retaliation.
The whole community waits seven days for Miriam. Temporary exclusion does not become abandonment.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 12 to silence women, punish criticism of leaders, defend racism, reject interracial families, stigmatize skin disease, or claim that illness proves Divine displeasure. Preserve the narrative while centering healing, communal waiting, and critical attention to its gender asymmetry.
